findings.phase_name: OWASP A02: Cryptographic Failures & A07: Authentication
findings.title: Unconditional Fallback to Hardcoded Secret in Client Portal JWT Verification
findings.description: portalAuth.ts sets a hardcoded default JWT secret string when process.env.JWT_SECRET is unset. In getPortalClient(), any JWT token signed with this hardcoded secret is accepted, allowing full authentication bypass.
findings.exploit_scenario: Attacker crafts a JWT containing any target clientId in the payload, signs it using the hardcoded secret 'ko-broker-portal-super-secret-key-for-local-dev-12345!', and sets it as the 'client_session' cookie. getPortalClient() validates the token via verifyToken() and grants full access to the borrower's case, financial details, and PII.
findings.impact: Complete unauthorized access to any borrower's portal account, financial data, and personal documents.
findings.recommendation: Enforce that JWT_SECRET is strictly required in all non-test environments. If process.env.JWT_SECRET is missing, fail-closed by rejecting verification or throwing a configuration error rather than falling back to a static string.

findings.title: Unsigned Stripe Webhook Execution when STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET is Unset
findings.description: When STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET is missing, the Stripe webhook route logs a warning and proceeds to execute handleEvent() on untrusted, unverified JSON input.
findings.exploit_scenario: Attacker posts a forged checkout.session.completed or customer.subscription.updated payload directly to /api/webhooks/stripe with metadata.orgId set to their organization. The system processes the event without cryptographic verification and elevates the organization's subscription plan to ENTERPRISE.
findings.impact: Unauthorized subscription plan elevation, bypassing Stripe payment collection.
findings.recommendation: Fail-closed: If STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET or the stripe-signature header is missing, return HTTP 400/401 immediately. Never process webhooks without signature validation.

findings.title: Inbound Email Webhook Allows Unsigned Message Injection
findings.description: If RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET and INBOUND_EMAIL_WEBHOOK_SECRET are unset, the route logs a warning and processes the email without cryptographic verification, creating new Message records.
findings.exploit_scenario: Attacker sends an unsigned HTTP POST request with a victim client's email address in payload.from.email. The route queries the client and case records and inserts a synthetic INBOUND message into the case timeline, spoofing borrower communications and corrupting audit logs.
findings.impact: Falsification of borrower communications and corruption of case history and compliance records.
findings.recommendation: Reject requests with 401 Unauthorized if webhook secret headers are absent or verification fails.

findings.phase_name: OWASP A01: Broken Access Control & A05: Misconfiguration
findings.title: CSRF Exposure via SameSite=None Portal Session Cookie
findings.description: Portal session cookies use sameSite: 'none' in production without CSRF token verification on state-changing PUT/POST endpoints.
findings.exploit_scenario: A borrower logs into their client portal. They subsequently visit an attacker-controlled site. The site issues a background cross-origin PUT request to /api/portal/fact-find. Because sameSite is 'none', the browser attaches client_session, allowing the attacker to tamper with fact-find form values.
findings.impact: Unauthorized modification of client fact-find responses or sending unauthorized messages via CSRF.
findings.recommendation: Switch sameSite to 'lax' or 'strict' if the frontend and API share the domain/subdomain, or implement standard anti-CSRF token verification / Sec-Fetch-Site checking on mutation routes.

findings.title: Next.js 16.2.4 Vulnerabilities (GHSA-2xp9-vwfh-vxw4, GHSA-p293-qw3h-jr36)
findings.description: The current version of Next.js (16.2.4) has known high and critical severity advisories including unauthenticated Remote Code Execution in the Image Optimization API when AVIF files are processed, and cache poisoning.
findings.exploit_scenario: Attacker sends crafted image requests to Next.js image optimization endpoint to trigger memory corruption or remote execution.
findings.impact: Server compromise or cache poisoning affecting multiple users.
findings.recommendation: Upgrade 'next' from 16.2.4 to the latest patched version (>= 16.3.3 or latest 16.x release).

findings.title: Missing .dockerignore Allows Local Secrets in Container Layers
findings.description: The repository lacks a .dockerignore file. When Dockerfile runs 'COPY . .', all local uncommitted files (.env, .env.local, .git) are included in the build context.
findings.exploit_scenario: Developer or automated pipeline builds the Docker image locally. Local .env or .git files are copied into the builder stage, persisting sensitive environment variables in layer history.
findings.impact: Leakage of development and production credentials in container images.
findings.recommendation: Create a root .dockerignore excluding .env*, node_modules, .git, and build artifacts.
